items.originalTitle: George Russell makes defiant Mercedes statement as Kimi Antonelli nears world title
detailZh: 乔治·拉塞尔在基米·安东内利接近世界冠军时发表坚定言论
梅赛德斯车手表示，尽管在2026年被队友基米·安东内利超越，但他仍认为自己在一级方程式赛车上还有“12到15年的好时光”
对于梅赛德斯车迷来说，这里是关于银箭的最新消息，包括来自布拉克利和布里克斯沃斯的F1新闻、车手更新、赛车发展和比赛分析。
梅赛德斯一级方程式车手乔治·拉塞尔坚称，尽管2026赛季表现不稳定，但他仍认为自己在锦标赛上还有“12到15年的好时光”。这位英国人在墨西哥城排名第二，尽管比他的年轻队友基米·安东内利少123分，但安东内利本周末有望赢得他的首个冠军头衔。
拉塞尔在澳大利亚赢得了赛季开门红，但他的这一年却在这之间摇摆不定，有 pole 和 wins，也有糟糕的结果，还因为可靠性问题退出了三次。另一方面，安东内利则表现得更加稳定。
‘坦白说，我觉得自己今年可能学到了比我想象中更多的东西，’ 拉塞尔承认。‘你在体育中经历的起伏是巨大的。这是因为我们都非常关心我们所做的事情。但我会提醒自己，我已经28岁了。我看到刘易斯在41岁时仍然表现出色，费尔南多在[45]岁。’
‘刘易斯在30多岁时赢得了他大多数的冠军。今年绝对不会定义我整个职业生涯。它不会让我崩溃。如果有什么的话，它只会让我变得更强大。’
尽管输给了只参加了他F1生涯第二个赛季的车手，而他自己已经参加了第八个赛季，但拉塞尔在回应方面表现得非常出色。
“我一直很自豪我的韧性和我从非常艰难的时刻中反弹回来的能力。实际上，在这个赛季的低谷时期，我通常都表现得非常强劲。然后我在一场好比赛之后又经历了一场糟糕的比赛。”
“所以也许这也是我需要分析的事情，因为我总是在最糟糕的比赛之后表现最好，这……可能只是巧合。也许其中有些东西，但我生命中参加比赛的时间比我没参加比赛的时间要多。我成功的年份比相对失败的年份要多。”
““我认为没有任何运动员，无论多么伟大，都能在他们的整个职业生涯中每年都达到最高水平。不幸的是，对我来说，今年可能是我最需要的时候。但这绝对不是我的旅程的终点。我还有12到15年的好时光。”"
“这位车手在巴库的压倒性胜利和马来西亚的DNS之后，在新加坡和奥斯汀分别获得了第九和第八名。这当然不容易。”"
“我们不是拳击手，在拳击场上直接与对手对抗。我们更像是在与自己的战斗，有点像高尔夫球手在资格赛圈中，你独自一人。而你的工作和准备决定了你的表现是否出色。”
"所以，我并不是直接看着我的头号竞争对手想，我该如何打败这个人？更多的是我在镜子前看着自己，思考我需要做什么才能避免这些糟糕的表现？"
也不会因为获得第二名而给他带来多少安慰：
"对于赛道上的每一位车手来说，只有一个位置是重要的，那就是第一名。成为剩下的人中的最佳者并不是你小时候的梦想。只要不是第一名，在这个运动中，这几乎就是一切或什么都没有。”
detailEn: George Russell makes defiant Mercedes statement as Kimi Antonelli nears world title
Mercedes driver says he still has “a good 12 to 15 years” left in Formula 1, despite being outperformed by team-mate Kimi Antonelli in 2026
For Mercedes fans. All the latest from the Silver Arrows, with F1 news, driver updates, car development and race analysis from Brackley and Brixworth.

Mercedes Formula 1 driver George Russell has insisted that, despite an inconsistent 2026 season, he still has “a good 12 to 15 years” left in the championship. The Briton arrives in Mexico City second in the drivers' standings, albeit 123 points off his young team-mate Kimi Antonelli, who can take his first championship title this weekend.

Russell won the season opener in Australia, but his year has since swung between poles and wins and poor results, with three retirements from reliability problems. Antonelli, on the other hand, has been far more consistent.

"I’ve probably learned more about myself this year than I would have liked to, in all honesty," Russell admitted. "The highs and lows you go through in sport are immense. And that’s because we all care so much for what we’re doing. But I remind myself, I’m 28 years old. I see Lewis still competing extremely well at 41 and Fernando at [45].
"Lewis won the majority of his titles in his 30s. And this year is absolutely not going to define my career as a whole. It’s not going to break me. If anything, it’s going to make me stronger."
Despite losing out to a driver who is only in his second season of his F1 career compared to his eighth, Russell has been exceptionally strong in his response.

“I’ve been pretty proud of my resilience and how I’ve bounced back from very tough moments. And actually, through my lowest points of this season, I’ve generally bounced back really, really strong. And then I had another bad race after the good one.

"So maybe it’s something I need to analyse as well, because I always perform best after my worst races, which is... maybe it’s just a coincidence. Maybe there’s something in it, but I’ve been racing more years of my life than I haven’t. And I’ve had more successful years than relative failures.

“And I don’t think any athlete, no matter how great, has every single year of their career performing at their highest level. Unfortunately, this year for me has come at maybe the time when I needed it most. But it’s by no means the end of my journey. I still got a good 12 to 15 years left in me.”
The driver finished ninth and eighth in Singapore and Austin respectively following a dominant win in Baku and a DNF in Malaysia. It certainly hasn't been easy.

“We’re not boxers where you’re in a ring fighting directly against somebody else. We are kind of fighting against ourselves, almost like a golfer in a way, a qualifying lap. You’re there by yourself. And it’s the work and preparation that you’ve done yourself that makes the difference to a good performance or not.

"So I’m not directly looking at my number one competitor saying, how am I going to beat this guy? It’s more I’m looking at myself in the mirror thinking, what do I need to do to not have these poor performances?”
Nor will finishing runner-up offer him much comfort:

“For every driver on the grid, there’s only one position that matters and it’s P1. And to be best of the rest is not really something you dream of as a kid. As long as it’s not P1 in this sport, it’s kind of that or nothing, really.”

items.originalTitle: George Russell warns Ferrari could have major advantage at Mexican GP
items.summaryEn: Mercedes driver George Russell believes Ferrari's smaller turbo could give it an advantage at the Mexican Grand Prix. The Mexico City circuit sits more than 2200 metres above sea level, where thin air reduces downforce and cooling and forces turbochargers to work harder to feed the engine.
detailZh: 拉塞尔警告法拉利可能在墨西哥大奖赛占据重大优势
拉塞尔认为法拉利较小的涡轮可能在墨西哥大奖赛带来优势
刘易斯·汉密尔顿、法拉利、乔治·拉塞尔、梅赛德斯
致梅赛德斯车迷。来自银箭的最新消息，包括F1新闻、车手动态、赛车研发以及来自布拉克利和布里克斯沃思的比赛分析。
梅赛德斯一级方程式车手乔治·拉塞尔认为，法拉利更小的涡轮可能在本次高海拔的罗德里格斯兄弟赛道举行的墨西哥大奖赛上给其带来优势。
墨西哥城赛道海拔超过2200米。稀薄空气会降低下压力和冷却效果，并迫使涡轮增压器更费力地为发动机供气。
在墨西哥车手新闻发布会上接受媒体采访时，拉塞尔被问及海拔是否会让本周末变得困难。
“这会非常有趣，”他说。“我认为涡轮迟滞本周末对很多车队来说都会是一个重要因素。显然这不是秘密，法拉利等车队的涡轮比大多数车队都小，所以他们在这方面可能相当有优势。”
“我们还不确定这会有多具挑战性，但可以肯定地预见它不会轻松。”
梅赛德斯也仍在努力理解其最新升级套件，这位28岁的车手在美国大奖赛上对此感到吃力。他在奥斯汀获得第八名，而他的队友、当前领跑积分榜的安东内利则赢得了本赛季第九个大奖赛冠军。
“自从我们把这一套件装上车后，对我们来说就有点奇怪，”拉塞尔补充道。“显然，我们最初是在马来西亚引入它，那对我们两人来说都是相当艰难的一个周末。然后基米在新加坡用上了它。同样，不是一个轻松的周末。
“我在奥斯汀重新用上了它，在我这边挣扎了很多。而他显然跑了一场非常强劲的比赛。我们在特性上看到的一些情况表明，它只在非常狭窄的窗口内发挥作用。所以我们需要努力拓宽这个窗口。”
拉塞尔目前在车手锦标赛中排名第二，落后安东内利123分，而安东内利有机会在本周末锁定冠军。
detailEn: George Russell warns Ferrari could have major advantage at Mexican GP
George Russell believes Ferrari's smaller turbo could give it an advantage at the Mexican Grand Prix
Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, George Russell, Mercedes
For Mercedes fans. All the latest from the Silver Arrows, with F1 news, driver updates, car development and race analysis from Brackley and Brixworth.
Mercedes Formula 1 driver George Russell believes Ferrari's smaller turbo could give it an advantage at this weekend's Mexican Grand Prix at the high-altitude Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez circuit.
The circuit in Mexico City sits more than 2200 metres above sea level. The thin air reduces downforce and cooling and forces turbochargers to work much harder to feed the engine.
While speaking to the media during the drivers' press conference in Mexico, Russell was asked whether the altitude would make this weekend difficult.

"It’s going to be very interesting," he said. "I think turbo lag is going to be a big factor for a lot of teams this weekend. There’s obviously no secret, the likes of Ferrari have a smaller turbo than most, so they probably have quite an advantage in this regard.
"We’re not sure as yet how challenging it will be, but can definitely foresee it being not straightforward."

Mercedes is also still trying to understand its latest upgrade package, which the 28-year-old struggled with at the United States Grand Prix. He finished eighth in Austin and his team-mate and current championship leader Kimi Antonelli claimed his ninth grand prix victory of the season.

"It’s been a little bit strange for us since we brought this package to the car," Russell added. "Obviously, we first brought it in Malaysia, and it was a pretty tough weekend for the two of us. And then Kimi had it on in Singapore. Again, not a straightforward weekend.

"I had it back on in Austin and struggled a lot on my side. And he obviously had a very strong race. And we are seeing some things in the characteristics that just show that it performed in a very narrow window. So we need to try and widen that."
Russell currently sits second in the drivers' championship, 123 points behind Antonelli, who has the opportunity to claim the title this weekend.
keyPointsZh: 高海拔迫使涡轮更费力地为发动机供气
keyPointsEn: The altitude forces turbochargers to work harder to feed the engine

items.originalTitle: 'Lack of talent' - Alonso doubles down on Albon criticism
items.summaryEn: Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso has doubled down on his criticism of "low level" Formula 1 drivers who have a "lack of talent" following his collision with Williams' Alex Albon in Austin.
detailZh: 费尔南多·阿隆索在墨西哥城大奖赛前再次批评亚历克斯·阿尔本以及F1赛场上的其他车手
两届F1世界冠军费尔南多·阿隆索重申了他对威廉姆斯车手亚历克斯·阿尔本以及其他在F1队尾竞争的车手的批评；天空体育F1将直播墨西哥城大奖赛的各节练习与排位，周五练习赛时间为18:30和22:00
阿斯顿·马丁车手费尔南多·阿隆索对F1中排名后三分之一车手的天赋水平提出了尖锐批评
阿斯顿·马丁车手费尔南多·阿隆索在奥斯汀与威廉姆斯车手亚历克斯·阿尔本发生碰撞后，再次批评F1中部分“水平低”“缺乏天赋”的车手。
在美国大奖赛的首圈，阿尔本试图在第11号发夹弯超越阿隆索升至第12位，但撞上了阿斯顿·马丁车手的侧面，导致两辆车都受损。
两位车手都没有受到处罚，两人都得以继续比赛，最终在奥斯汀阿隆索获得第16名，阿尔本获得第17名。
安东内利如何在周日的墨西哥城大奖赛上赢得世界冠军

赛后，阿隆索表示F1发车区后三分之一车手的质量“非常低”，在本周末墨西哥城大奖赛前的周四媒体日上，他并未改变自己的立场。
“我认为这纯粹是驾驶水平非常低，缺乏天赋，”他告诉天空体育F1。
“当你在整个赛季中反复犯错，发生撞车，且50%的比赛在第一圈就结束了，如果我是车队领队，我不会高兴，但如果他们高兴，我也没问题。”
“当我看到马克斯（维斯塔潘）、刘易斯（汉密尔顿）在更换引擎或其他原因后从后排起步时，还有基米在蒙扎，他们依然能赢下比赛。当你拥有自信和天赋，愿意再多等一两圈时，第一圈并不是世界末日。”
2026年美国大奖赛精彩集锦
阿隆索表示，他不会在周五的车手会议上提出这个问题，因为“这是比赛的一部分”，而且这取决于阿斯顿·马丁能否从更靠前的位置发车，从而“摆脱那个区域”。
“有些车队无法得分。今年对我们来说也是一样。你参加比赛时就知道，需要八次退赛才能得分，所以更重要的是跑出最好的比赛直到终点线，”他补充道。
"如果你赛季表现不佳，被队友击败，无论你脑子里在想什么，都会带来额外的挫败感，但其他车手和车队不应该为此付出代价。"
费尔南多·阿隆索在奥斯汀与亚历克斯·阿尔本发生碰撞后，批评了"低水平的后三分之一车手"
"听到这样的话不太好受"——阿尔本回应阿隆索的言论
阿尔本在国际汽联新闻发布会上得知了阿隆索的言论，并辩称目前的发车阵容"有一段时间"以来从未如此强大。
威廉姆斯车手表示：“我也要加倍坚持我之前的说法。我对费尔南多怀有极大的敬意。我小时候非常仰慕他。”
“从很多方面来说，听到那些评论并不好受。你正在和你仰慕的人比赛，但与此同时，我并不同意。就这么简单。”
“我认为发车区上下水平的实力都很强。我认为10年、15年前，发车区后半部分的状况和现在不一样。我们不再有付费车手了。事情就是这样。希望这个周末的比赛中我们不会在弯角或赛道上相遇！”
威廉姆斯车手亚历克斯·阿尔本不同意费尔南多·阿隆索关于一级方程式发车区后三分之一存在“缺乏天赋”的说法
不过，阿隆索指出，自从他2001年首次亮相F1以来，他的这些评论在他职业生涯的任何阶段都会是一样的。
“多年来都是如此。当你在发车区后排时，赛车很难驾驶，更难驾驶——它们抓地力更小，所以失误更频繁，因为你没有一个受控的环境，赛车也不会以友好的方式迎接你，所以你会犯更多错误。
“但我不觉得第一圈的所有事故和碰撞、飞来飞去的前翼，所有这些事情都是不必要的，尤其是当你在发车区后排毫无意义地争斗时，还有预算帽，让这个问题雪上加霜。
“有些车队对预算帽很满意，每场比赛都撞坏东西。他们付得起。”

detailEn: Fernando Alonso doubles down on Alex Albon and F1 field criticism ahead of Mexico City Grand Prix

Two-time F1 world champion Fernando Alonso has reiterated his criticism of Williams' Alex Albon and other drivers who battle at the back of the grid in F1; watch every session of the Mexico City GP with Friday's practice sessions at 6.30pm and 10pm, live on Sky Sports F1
Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso was scathing in his assessment of the talent level of the lower third of the Formula 1 grid
Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso has doubled down on his criticism of "low level" Formula 1 drivers who have a "lack of talent" following his collision with Williams' Alex Albon in Austin.
Albon tried to overtake Alonso for 12th place into the Turn 11 hairpin on the opening lap of the United States Grand Prix, but went into the side of the Aston Martin driver, damaging both cars.
Neither driver received a penalty and both were able to continue with Alonso finishing 16th and Albon in 17th in Austin.

Post-race, Alonso stated the quality of the drivers in the bottom third of F1's grid is "very low" and he had not changed his stance in Thursday's media day ahead of this weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix.
"I think it's simply a very low level of driving and lack of talent," he told Sky Sports F1.

"When you make repeated mistakes throughout the season and have crashes and 50 per cent of your race is in Lap 1, if I was the team principal I would not be happy but if they are happy, I'm OK with that.

"When I see Max [Verstappen], Lewis [Hamilton] starting at the back when they change the engine or whatever, Kimi in Monza, they still win the races. Lap 1 is not the end of the world when you have your confidence and the talent to wait for one or two more laps."
Highlights from the 2026 United States Grand Prix
Alonso says he will not bring up the issue in Friday's drivers' meeting as "it's part of the game" and it is down to Aston Martin to start higher up the grid to "get out of that part of the field".

"Some teams cannot score points. It's the same for us this year. You go into the races knowing you need eight DNFs to score points, so it's more about driving the best race to the finish line," he added.
"Probably if you're not having a good season, being beaten by your team-mate, whatever is in your head it brings extra frustration but other drivers and teams should not pay for that."
Fernando Alonso criticised 'low quality bottom third drivers' following his collision with Alex Albon in Austin
'Not nice to hear that' - Albon reacts to Alonso comments
Albon was told about Alonso's comments in the FIA press conference and argued the grid is as strong as it has been "for a while".
"I'll double down with what I said as well. I have a huge respect for Fernando. I looked up to him a lot growing up as a kid," said the Williams driver.
"It's not nice to hear those comments in many ways. You're racing someone that you look up to, but at the same time, I don't agree. It's as simple as that.

"I think level is strong up and down the grid. I think 10, 15 years ago, the back half the grid wasn't the way it is now. We don't have pay drivers anymore. It is what it is. Hopefully, we don't cross corners or cross paths in the race this weekend!"
Williams driver Alex Albon disagrees with Fernando Alonso's assertion that there's a 'lack of talent' in the lower third of the Formula 1 grid
However, Alonso had pointed out his comments would be the same at any point in his career since he made his F1 debut in 2001.

"It's the same over the years. When you are at the back of the grid, the cars are difficult to drive, more difficult to drive - they have less grip so mistakes are coming more often because you don't have an environment which is under control and the car is not welcoming you in a nice way, so you make more mistakes.

"But I don't feel all the incidents in Lap 1 and the touches, the front wings that fly around, all these things are not necessary, especially when you are fighting for nothing at the back of the grid and there is the cost cap, adding to this problem.
"There are teams that are happy with the cost cap and breaking things every race. They can pay for them."

media.altZh: 拉塞尔：今年失冠不会击垮我 · 第 1 张

items.originalTitle: George Russell on F1 title loss: 'This year won't break me'
items.summaryEn: George Russell has said that failing to win his first Formula 1 world title this season will not define his career or break him. His Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli enters the Mexico Grand Prix on the verge of becoming F1 champion.
detailZh: 拉塞尔：今年失冠不会击垮我
随着梅赛德斯队友安东内利在进入墨西哥大奖赛时接近成为F1世界冠军，拉塞尔展现出不服输的态度
拉塞尔表示，本赛季未能夺得个人首个F1世界冠军不会定义他的职业生涯，也不会击垮他。
这位英国车手进入本赛季时是车手世界冠军的明显热门；他职业生涯初期驾驶处于队尾的威廉姆斯赛车时表现出色，之后在梅赛德斯难以重现地效时代此前统治力的情况下升入该队，并继续引人注目。
但那种偏袒并未成为现实，银箭队友基米·安东内利有望在本周末的墨西哥城大奖赛上成为F1最年轻的世界冠军——拉塞尔必须赢下这场比赛，才有任何希望推迟那不可避免的结局。
尽管糟糕的可靠性在一定程度上阻碍了拉塞尔对这位意大利人发起真正的冠军挑战，但他自己的表现有时也未能达到安东内利所设定的水准。
安东内利在第二个赛季已斩获九场分站胜利，而拉塞尔尽管在赛季揭幕的澳大利亚大奖赛上以统治性方式夺冠，却只赢了三场；不过他在罗德里格斯兄弟赛道表示，前队友刘易斯·汉密尔顿和阿斯顿·马丁的费尔南多·阿隆索就是证明——本赛季未能拿下车手总冠军并不意味着梦想就此终结。
“说实话，今年我对自己有了更多了解，可能比我原本想要的还要多，”拉塞尔承认道。
在体育运动中，你所经历的高潮和低谷是巨大的，那是因为我们都非常在乎自己所做的事情。
但我提醒自己，我才28岁。我看到刘易斯·汉密尔顿在41岁、费尔南多·阿隆索在44岁仍然竞争得非常出色。你知道，刘易斯的大部分冠军都是在30多岁时赢得的，而今年绝对不会定义我整个职业生涯。它不会击垮我。如果说有什么影响，那只会让我更强大。
我一直相当为自己的韧性感到自豪，以及我如何从非常艰难的时刻中反弹回来，而实际上，在本赛季我最低谷的时刻，我总体上反弹得非常非常强劲——然后在一场好比赛之后我又经历了一场糟糕的比赛。
所以也许这也是我需要分析的事情，因为我总是在最糟糕的比赛之后表现最好，也许这只是巧合。也许其中有些道理，但我人生中参加赛车的年份比不参赛的年份更多，而且我成功的年份相对失败而言也更多。
“而且我认为任何运动员，无论多么伟大，都不可能在自己职业生涯的每一年都保持最高水平。不幸的是，对我来说，今年恰好是在我最需要的时候到来了。但这绝不是我的旅程的终点。”
“我体内还有12到15年的好时光。”
虽然冠军实际上可能已掌握在安东内利手中，但拉塞尔仍决心利用本赛季最后几场比赛来克服任何问题，以高昂姿态结束赛季，为2027年的冲击做好准备。
当被问及前梅赛德斯车手尼科·罗斯伯格在2015年赢得最后三场比赛，随后在下一个赛季成为冠军时，拉塞尔回答说：“我认为努力保持一定的稳定性对我来说绝对很重要。”
“几场比赛之前（阿塞拜疆），我们以零点八秒的优势拿到杆位并赢下比赛，然后上周我以第八名完赛。我职业生涯中从未有过表现波动如此之大的赛季，我知道这种能力还在，因为如果你所谓的‘丢了手感’，是不可能在巴库交出那样的表现的。
只是我们很难保持高命中率。我们不知道原因何在，以前也从未遇到过。我个人职业生涯中从未有过这种情况，我想这大概是我在最后这几场比赛中的首要任务。”
detailEn: George Russell on F1 title loss: 'This year won't break me'
Russell is in a defiant mood as Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli enters the Mexico GP on the verge of becoming F1 champion
George Russell has insisted his career will 'not be defined' and he 'won't be broken' by failing to secure a maiden Formula 1 world title this season.

The British driver entered the campaign as clear favourite for the drivers' championship having impressed in a back-of-the-grid Williams to begin his career, before continuing to catch the eye when stepping up to Mercedes as the team struggled to replicate previous dominance during the ground-effect era.

But that favouritism hasn't become reality, with Silver Arrows team-mate Kimi Antonelli on the verge of becoming F1's youngest champion at this weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix - a race Russell has to win to have any hope of delaying the inevitable.

And while poor reliability has played its part in stopping Russell from putting down a genuine title challenge to the Italian, his own performances have sometimes failed to live up to the mark Antonelli has set.

While Antonelli has picked up nine race wins in his second year, Russell has managed only three despite winning in dominant fashion at the season-opening Australian GP but speaking at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, he pointed to former team-mate Lewis Hamilton and Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso as proof that the failure to take the drivers' crown this term doesn't mean the dream is over.
"I've probably learned more about myself this year than I would have liked to, in all honesty," Russell conceded.
"The highs and lows you go through in sport are immense and that's because we all care so much for what we're doing.

"But I remind myself, I'm 28 years old. I see Lewis [Hamilton] still competing extremely well at 41 and Fernando [Alonso] at 44. You know, Lewis won the majority of his titles in his 30s and this year is absolutely not going to define my career as a whole. It's not going to break me. If anything, it's going to make me stronger.

"I've been pretty proud of my resilience and how I've bounced back from very tough moments and actually, through my lowest points of this season, I've generally bounced back really, really strong - and then I had another bad race after the good one.

"So maybe it's something I need to analyse as well, because I always perform best after my worst races, maybe it's just a coincidence. Maybe there's something in it, but I've been racing more years of my life than I haven't and I've had more successful years than relative failures.

"And I don't think any athlete, no matter how great, has every single year of their career performing at their highest level. Unfortunately, this year for me has come at maybe the time when I needed it most. But it's by no means the end of my journey.
"I've still got a good 12 to 15 years left in me."

While the championship may effectively be in Antonelli's hands, Russell is still determined to use the final races of the current campaign to overcome any issues and end the season on a high, ready for a 2027 assault.

Put to him that former Mercedes driver Nico Rosberg won the final three races in 2015 before going on to become champion the following season, Russell replied: "I think it is definitely important for me to try and gain some consistency.

"A couple of races ago [Azerbaijan], we were on pole by eight tenths and won the race, and then last week I finished in P8. I've never had a season like this in my career where the performance has fluctuated so much and I know it's in there, because you can't deliver performances like that in Baku if you've so-called lost it.

"It's just that we're struggling to have a high hit rate. We don't know why that is, and we've never had it. I've never had it personally before in my career, and I guess that's probably the priority for me in these last few races."
